sections.heading: 1. Make it comfortable
lines: ① Mention heart issues, surgery, bones, meds.
② Ask for lighter pressure any time.
③ Try side-lying or seated if face down is hard.
④ Get on and off the table slowly, with help.

sections.heading: 2. Pair it with movement
lines: help keep you steady on your feet.

caption:
Koko has stiff shoulders after a day in the garden and is thinking about her first massage.

Start by telling your therapist about heart conditions, recent surgery, osteoporosis, diabetes and any medications. It helps them choose pressure and position. Skin can bruise more easily as we age, so moderate pressure often feels great and still eases stiffness. Side-lying or seated positions are options too.

Massage can ease stiffness, and it works well alongside walking, strength and balance work. New calf pain or swelling, chest pain or breathlessness means a GP visit first.

Our remedial massage therapists at Hybrid Physio adjust pressure and pace to suit you. Book online via the link in bio.
